timestamp_derivation: After the four content commits were written, built and tested, and after the live PRE-LIVE privilege probe that decided how the Gate-P gaps were closed. Before the commit that carries this receipt.
authorisation: Product-Owner closure mission, recorded at T0175 and reconciled into the authoritative state by this increment.

the_contradiction_this_increment_had_to_.what: next_authorized_action read 'NONE is authorized ... No Room Login, no guest activation, no PMS configuration change, no Full Resync, no financial traffic, no deployment, no migration, no service restart and no Go-Live is authorized' while T0175, in the same file, recorded the Product Owner's end-to-end authorisation for controlled PRE-LIVE work including deployment, migrations, service restarts and recovery drills.
the_contradiction_this_increment_had_to_.why_it_mattered: Both cannot be true, and the field that says what is authorised is the first thing any agent or operator reads. Left as it was, the closure would have been unrecognisable in the record as authorised work -- and the next session would have been correct to refuse it.
the_contradiction_this_increment_had_to_.how_resolved: The mission authorisation is the later and more specific statement and now stands. next_authorized_action names ONE action (the validator enforces that, and the first attempt was correctly refused as 'not a single action'), with the detail moved to allowed_actions, prohibited_actions and a new current_state_facts.functional_completeness_remaining.
the_contradiction_this_increment_had_to_.what_did_not_change: Real Guest activation and Guest pilot use stay DEFERRED by D41. Real PMS financial posting, real payment-provider traffic, real settlement, real reversal and paid Guest activation stay PROHIBITED. Go-Live stays NOT AUTHORISED. 172.21.60.23 must not be contacted.
the_contradiction_this_increment_had_to_.a_prohibition_recorded_as_satisfied_rath: prohibited_actions carried a D35-era clause forbidding 'deploying to any new server before the Product Owner provides that server and authorizes execution on it'. That server was provided and commissioned as PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25 under D37/T0087, so the clause is satisfied. Reclassifying 172.21.60.23, retiring the development legacy baseline, and cloning development state onto PRE-LIVE all remain prohibited.

gatep_grant_durability.severity: HIGH, and nine of them were broken on the live appliance rather than only on a rebuild
gatep_grant_durability.what: T0175 enumerated 40 service-role grants that migrations make and deploy/gatep/ does not, so they do not survive a factory-clean install: gatep-grants.sql revokes ALL privileges from the service roles and runs AFTER the numbered migrations.
gatep_grant_durability.method_that_made_it_safe: Every one was probed against PRE-LIVE before a single GRANT was written. That turned a bulk guess into a reproduction of the appliance's real privilege state, and it is what produced the finding below.
gatep_grant_durability.what_the_probe_found: 29 PRESENT on PRE-LIVE (the PMS roster-reconciliation subsystem). 9 ABSENT WITH THEIR OBJECTS PRESENT -- svc_scd's p6_guest_release_device, its policy function, appliance_product_settings and guest_device_actions; svc_edged's p6_set_guest_device_self_service and appliance_product_setting_changes; svc_acctd's session_online_watermarks, entitlement_devices and entitlement_termination_evidence. GUEST DEVICE SELF-SERVICE IS UNPRIVILEGED ON PRE-LIVE TODAY: a guest release would fail at the database rather than at the policy. It has gone unnoticed because the capability is DARK by deployment flag and default-OFF by setting, so nothing has ever called it. 2 DEAD: 0069 granted on iam_v2.pms_reoffer_stay_event and iam_v2.stay_event_reoffers, and 0070 drops both after refusing if the audit log holds rows.
gatep_grant_durability.a_correction_to_the_check_itself: The first probe could not tell a dropped object from a missing privilege: bool_or over zero rows returns NULL, a CASE on NULL takes the else branch, so a dropped function read as 'the role lacks EXECUTE'. The probe now counts rows first. The validator makes the same distinction by reading the generated baseline -- a dump of the END STATE of the whole chain, regenerated by any delivery that changes a migration and proven against the upgrade path object for object -- so an object absent from it is absent at the end, established from the tree with no database.
gatep_grant_durability.proof: 38 mirrored into the per-service Gate-P files with their reasoning. The regenerated baseline goes from 323 GRANT lines to 373, and both install paths still agree: 9590 catalog facts, IDENTICAL, up from 9552. The validator's exception list is now EMPTY and the mechanism stays, so a future migration that grants without mirroring fails immediately.
gatep_grant_durability.not_yet_done: The nine live-broken grants are restored on the appliance by running the authoritative Gate-P reconcile there. That is a deployment action and belongs with the live drills, not with a commit.

guarded_down_migration_runner.severity: HIGH -- the documented rollback was unexecutable
guarded_down_migration_runner.what: scripts/edge-migrate.sh had no --down. docs/PHASE3_DEPLOYMENT_AND_ROLLBACK_RUNBOOK.md printed the command and the runner answered 'REFUSED: unknown arg: --down' and exit 2; the string 'down' did not appear in the file. So a live schema rollback was a hand-run psql outside every guard, and an operator reaching that step mid-incident would have improvised around one.
guarded_down_migration_runner.four_guards_a_forward_apply_does_not_nee: --ack-down, a SECOND acknowledgement with its own vocabulary per kind, because --ack-target says which database you mean and --ack-down says you mean to REMOVE schema from it: an operator who has typed the apply ack a hundred times must not be one flag away from dropping a schema. HEAD-OF-LEDGER, because rolling back 0060 while 0085 is applied leaves everything between standing on objects that no longer exist and a down script only knows how to undo itself. THE OPPOSITE LEDGER PRIVILEGE -- SELECT + DELETE, which the forward path REFUSES on a live site, so the role that migrates forward cannot roll back by construction. And --all is refused, because a down sweep is a schema deletion with a loop around it.
guarded_down_migration_runner.the_inverted_on_error_stop_reasoning: Without forced ON_ERROR_STOP a FAILED down still reaches the appended ledger DELETE: the body's COMMIT degrades to ROLLBACK so the objects SURVIVE, and the DELETE then commits in its own implicit transaction. The database would hold objects its ledger denies, and the next forward apply would try to create what is already there. Both proofs are required: psql's exit status, and the ledger row actually being gone.
guarded_down_migration_runner.what_it_does_not_do: Take a backup, or claim to have verified one. An acknowledgement flag the script could not check would be theatre rather than a guard, so the backup is a runbook step.
guarded_down_migration_runner.proof: Fourteen cases added to the existing disposable-Postgres self-test, which the phase3 gate already runs; the suite is now 28 cases. The rollback removing both object and ledger row, THE RE-APPLY AFTERWARDS (a rollback that cannot be re-applied is a one-way door), and eleven refusals.
guarded_down_migration_runner.a_case_that_failed_first_and_was_worth_h: The rollback role could not drop a table the apply role owned -- 'must be owner of table' -- and the runner refused, reported psql exit 3, and left BOTH the object and the ledger row intact. That is the failing-down property arriving unprompted in the happy-path case. The fixture now models what the appliance models: the rollback/admin role administers what the apply role created.

nightly_backup_scheduler.what: docs/BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md said a backup agent runs the site backup nightly, and set a nightly policy. There was no agent: nothing under deploy/ invoked the script, no cron entry existed, and the only backup-related unit PRUNES artefacts and creates none. Every backup this appliance has ever had was taken by a human typing the command while the document stated a schedule.
nightly_backup_scheduler.fix: stayconnect-site-backup.{service,timer}. 02:10 LOCAL, not UTC, because the policy is a low-traffic hour in the site's timezone and a hotel's quiet hour is a property of where the hotel is -- and it is before the 03:30 retention cleanup, so a night's backup exists before retention runs and the newest full backup the cleanup protects is the one just taken. Persistent=true so an appliance powered off overnight does not skip a day in silence. Type=oneshot with NO Restart: a failed backup is a fact for an operator to see, and a retry loop on a full disk makes the disk worse.
nightly_backup_scheduler.the_script_remains_the_guard: It refuses on its own -- no resolvable role, a client older than the server, an empty dump, and an /etc archive containing the financial restore marker, which it verifies by LISTING the archive rather than trusting the --exclude.
nightly_backup_scheduler.installation_needed_no_list: install-service-units.sh derives every /opt/stayconnect/bin helper from the units being installed and REFUSES the whole install if one has no source. That rule exists because a hand-written list once omitted stayconnect-backup-cleanup.service: it failed 203/EXEC nightly for weeks, artefacts accumulated until the root filesystem hit 100%, PostgreSQL could not write postmaster.pid, and the site went down. The new unit is picked up by that mechanism and install-service-units-selftest.sh reports it.

financial_restore_rollback_detector.severity: HIGH in principle, zero in effect today, and both halves were inert
financial_restore_rollback_detector.what: Migration 0023 exists to notice that this database is older than the appliance knows it should be, because it was restored. payment.ReconcileEpoch is the process half and its own comment states the ordering rule: it runs BEFORE any financial worker starts. NOTHING CALLED IT -- a grep outside tests returned its own definition and two comments about itself.
financial_restore_rollback_detector.fix: edged runs it at startup, after the flags are loaded and before any route is mounted. edged is the only process that constructs a financial engine at all, so it is the only one with a financial worker to run before. A test asserts the ordering against main.go's source.
financial_restore_rollback_detector.failure_posture_mirrors_an_existing_prec: Phase 3's controlled-writer boundary is verified by every writing service before it serves anything and EXITS if it does not hold, but only with the flags ON. Same rule: while Phase 4 is DARK a failed reconcile is logged loudly and startup continues, because nothing is protected by refusing to serve the whole operator API for money that cannot move; once transmission is on, a failed reconcile EXITS, because not knowing whether this is restored data is the exact condition 0023 exists to stop. The dark message says the detector DID NOT RUN rather than that it found nothing -- different claims, and a test pins the wording so it cannot be softened.
financial_restore_rollback_detector.a_test_expectation_that_was_wrong: I expected master+transmit to be non-dark. TransmitOn requires THREE flags -- master AND outbox AND transmit -- and says why: 'so no single mis-set variable can put financial bytes on a wire'. The test was corrected, not the code, and the three-flag rule is now pinned including that all-three is the only non-dark combination.
financial_restore_rollback_detector.still_open: The management marker is uninitialised. That is a recorded PRE-FINANCIAL-ENABLE PREREQUISITE and initialising it needs the supported restore process on the appliance, so it belongs with the live drills.

what_this_increment_did_not_do: Nothing was deployed. No binary was built for an appliance, no service restarted, no migration applied anywhere live, and no Gate-P reconcile run on the appliance. The only PRE-LIVE access was a read-only privilege probe -- has_table_privilege, has_function_privilege and catalog lookups -- which is what decided how the Gate-P gaps were closed.
financial_traffic: ZERO and untouched. This increment wires a DETECTOR that can only cause more holding; nothing in its path releases a hold, clears an epoch, or moves money.
still_open_after_this_increment: The voucher operator surface (issuance has no caller anywhere), voucher reveal/export, the financial marker initialisation, and every live drill: tagged multi-VLAN acceptance, Device Self-Service acceptance, backup/restore, schema rollback and forward recovery on the appliance, reboot verification, the Central-outage local-first drill, the security and recovery checks, and final full-system re-acceptance. Enumerated in current_state_facts.functional_completeness_remaining.
product_owner_decisions_unchanged: HA architecture (ARCH-04), payment-provider identity and commercial semantics, and the C35 external archival receipt authority remain decisions rather than gaps. The approving-review question remains open in open_product_owner_decisions.

the_gate_correction_this_receipt_also_ca.what_failed: The governance gate refused the first head with 'BASELINE FAIL: structural=0 keyword=1'. The adversarial mutation suite will not mutate anything until BOTH validators pass on the good state, and the keyword half -- tools/validate-project-state.sh, the Zero-Stale rule -- did not.
the_gate_correction_this_receipt_also_ca.why: That validator keeps an allowlist of recognised next_authorized_action phrases and requires the generated packs to state one of them in at least two places. This increment replaced the action with the FUNCTIONAL-COMPLETENESS CLOSURE wording, which the allowlist had never heard of, so the only remaining match in the packs was a HISTORICAL Phase-1B line and the count fell to one. A state file that had just been made truthful therefore read as inconsistent.
the_gate_correction_this_receipt_also_ca.the_fix_and_the_one_that_was_refused: The allowlist gained the current phrase. The alternative -- rewording next_authorized_action back to something the list already knew -- would have meant restoring the contradiction this increment exists to remove in order to satisfy a check about staleness. The comment above that allowlist already says why that is the wrong way round; it was written the last time the list lagged, for the same reason.
the_gate_correction_this_receipt_also_ca.the_second_defect_it_exposed: THE PREFLIGHT COULD NOT SEE IT. tools/validate-project-state.sh runs in the governance gate and in the mutation suite's baseline, and tools/preflight.sh ran neither -- so a one-alternative regex lag could only be learned on a runner, twenty minutes in, after every other gate step had been paid for. Preflight stage 9 now runs it, and tools/validate-delivery-protocol.py requires that stage to exist: the fifth entry in a list where every other entry is also a failure this project already paid for.
the_gate_correction_this_receipt_also_ca.what_it_cost: One governance cycle. The other three gates were ALL GREEN on the rejected head, which is recorded in current_delivery.first_rejected_head rather than erased.

the_review_round_and_what_it_found.summary: Four findings, all real, three of them defects this increment introduced. The other three gates were ALL GREEN on the reviewed head; none of these would have been caught by them.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.three_reversed_security_boundaries: Mirroring 'every grant a migration makes' into Gate-P restored three privileges migration 0034 DELIBERATELY REVOKED: svc_scd's EXECUTE on the three-argument p6_guest_release_device (whose parameterised throttle is the reason it is owner-only -- a caller can pass 2147483647), svc_scd's SELECT/INSERT on guest_device_actions (0034 refuses it by name as a 'speculative grant'), and svc_edged's SELECT/INSERT on appliance_product_setting_changes. Gate-P runs AFTER the migrations, so each was restored on every factory-clean install and every reconcile, and 0034's own assertions run at migration time and could not see it. The reviewer named one; the corrected validator found three. None is used by any Go source.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.the_validator_was_the_cause: validate-migration-grant-durability.py compared GRANTs to GRANTs, so a withdrawn privilege was indistinguishable from a durability gap. It now folds grants and revokes in file order and PER PRIVILEGE. Two of my own errors on the way: a coarse first version called svc_edged's SELECT on appliance_product_settings a reversal, where 0034 revokes only the writes; and the fix then reported PASS with all three reversals present, because collect() also runs for deploy/gatep/ and its paths sort last, so Gate-P's grants were folded into the migration timeline and cancelled every revoke.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.the_detector_could_not_be_called: edged connects as svc_edged (read from /etc/stayconnect/edged.env on PRE-LIVE). iam_v2.p4_reconcile_financial_epoch_v2 is granted only to sc_payment_runtime and svc_edged holds no membership -- both probed FALSE live. So the caller this increment added returned permission denied on every startup: the detector still did not run. Migration 0086 grants that ONE function to svc_edged, mirrors it into Gate-P, and asserts no membership and no table write was gained. NOT a financial enablement: the function's only outcomes hold money movement or change nothing.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.the_timer_would_never_have_fired: WantedBy=timers.target is an instruction for `systemctl enable`, not an effect, and install-service-units.sh only copied units and reloaded. Both timers on the appliance are enabled because somebody remembered; the nightly backup would have been the one nobody did. The installer now enables every timer it installs and requires systemd to name a next elapse.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.the_rollback_race: The head-of-ledger check ran before the advisory lock, and the lock key was derived from the version being reverted -- so a forward apply of a HIGHER version took a different key and could commit in between, and the under-lock recheck asked only whether the row still existed. Both directions now take one ledger-wide key first, in the same order, and the down path re-establishes head under the lock. EDGE_MIGRATE_SELFTEST = PASS (31 cases), including one that makes an apply wait 24s for a lock another session holds.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.live_access_this_round: READ-ONLY, on PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25 only: the two DSN usernames, two privilege probes, the timer list, and the absence of the financial restore marker. Nothing was written, deployed or restarted.
